Hi all, checking before I put time into PR formatting: does this exist under another name, and is it wanted?

The result. A continuous generalization of positive-definiteness to arbitrary kernels, no group structure needed:

lean

def PositiveDefiniteKernel {X : Type*} (K : X → X → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (s : Finset X) (c : X → ℂ),
    0 ≤ ∑ i ∈ s, ∑ j ∈ s, c i * conj (c j) * K i j

Main theorem, for X a compact (pseudo)metric space with probability measure μ, continuous Mercer-PD kernel K, continuous f:

lean

lemma PositiveDefiniteKernel.integralOperator_nonneg
    {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X]
    [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] [SecondCountableTopology X]
    (μ : Measure X) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    {K : X → X → ℂ} (hK : PositiveDefiniteKernel K)
    (hK_cont : Continuous (Function.uncurry K))
    {f : X → ℂ} (hf_cont : Continuous f) :
    0 ≤ ∫ x, ∫ y, f x * conj (f y) * K x y ∂μ ∂μ

Proved by Riemann-sum approximation controlled via uniform continuity (Heine-Cantor). Supporting suite: Hermitian symmetry, Schur/Hadamard product, composition, n-ary product, plus a group-theoretic version that reduces to this one.

Relation to existing Mathlib. Reproducing.lean has RKHS.posSemidef_kernel, the finite-matrix PSD condition. This is the continuous/measure-theoretic analogue: positivity as a double-integral inequality rather than a finite-matrix condition. I didn't find anything generalizing Reproducing.lean in that direction.

Absence check. grep on the pinned commit for PositiveDefiniteKernel, bare PositiveDefinite, integralOperator_nonneg: 0 matches. Loogle search for the 0 ≤ ∫∫ _*_*_ ∂_ ∂_ pattern: 0 matches. Not exhaustive, happy to be corrected.

API note. There's a functionally similar group-theoretic PD notion in the external repo Vilin97/lean-pool, bundled as a structure over AddGroup. I used a bare Prop over Group, closer to how Matrix.PosSemidef is phrased. Open to feedback either way.

#print axioms: only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. No sorry.

Can share the standalone files if useful.

That's Matrix.PosSemidef, the finite-matrix condition (also what Reproducing.lean's RKHS.posSemidef_kernel uses). Mine is the continuous analogue, a double integral over a measure space, ∫∫ f(x) conj(f(y)) K(x,y) dμ dμ ≥ 0, with the finite case appearing only internally as a building block via matrix_posSemidef.
I mean that your definition PositiveDefiniteKernel is equivalent to Matrix.PosSemidef and it would therefore be bett for you to use it

You're right, thanks, the definition is equivalent to ∀ s, PosSemidef on the submatrix and I should build it on top of Matrix.PosSemidef rather than reproving the finite case by hand, that'll likely simplify several of the supporting lemmas too. The part I think is actually new is the integral operator result over a continuous compact measure space (∫∫ f(x)·conj(f(y))·K(x,y) dμ dμ ≥ 0), which isn't expressible in terms of Matrix.PosSemidef since there's no finite matrix there. Will refactor the def and resubmit.
Do you really need the space to be compact and the function continuous? Can't you generalise to arbitrary integrable functions ?
Refactored PositiveDefiniteKernel to build on Matrix.PosSemidef on the finite submatrix, with the equivalence proved as quadratic_form_nonneg/of_quadratic_form. Still checking on the other.

Still digging into the generalization you flagged. Turns out it's true but needs a different proof technique than the compact case, so I'm working that out properly before submitting rather than sending something half-baked. Will follow up soon.

A design question that might be relevant is whether it should be defined as an double integral, like you have here, or as a single integral over the product measure. Whilst they are equivalent under a Fubini-Tonelli argument, it might safe some measurability proofs if you use one over the other. For example, I used the product measure in the construction of the integral operator in my draft PR #42003.
